external_primary_findings.title: Overcoming State Inertia in Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models via Activation Steering
external_primary_findings.finding: The paper identifies a transient generative-to-perceptive state lag during abrupt user interruption and introduces a Zero-Buffer Benchmark that measures immediate interruption comprehension with response correctness and initial-word occurrence rate.
external_primary_findings.f2_relevance: The mechanism is model-specific, but the failure shape is architecture-independent enough to falsify at the Frankenstein voice boundary: an interruption must not lose the semantically critical beginning of newly admitted user input while cancellation/reentry occurs.

external_primary_findings.title: What Did I Just Say? Self-Listening for Full-Duplex Speech Models
external_primary_findings.finding: The project describes playback-grounded self-listening that distinguishes generated model content from speech actually delivered to the user after interruption.
external_primary_findings.f2_relevance: This strongly corroborates the already-existing Frankenstein heard-prefix/playout-synchronization policy, but does not justify a duplicate handoff because Trigger7 has already routed heard-prefix conservation and playout-synced evidence requirements.

external_primary_findings.title: Multi-Faceted Interactivity Alignment in Full-Duplex Speech Models
external_primary_findings.finding: The paper separates interactive behavior into pause handling, turn-taking, backchanneling and user interruption and reports post-training improvements across those axes.
external_primary_findings.f2_relevance: Use the four-axis decomposition only as a coverage audit against existing deterministic F2 fixtures; add tests only for transition classes not already represented.
